narrative: Material PL1__M8952F4C exhibits moderate, continuous demand averaging 837.6 units per working day with a CV of 0.40 and a statistically significant upward trend. Lead times are stable at approximately 4.82 working days after removing 5 outlier observations including an erroneous 9,201-day entry. The recommended (r,Q) policy raises safety stock from 874 to 1,579 units to meet the 95% service level target, while the storage capacity of 22,674.9 units constrains the order quantity to 21,095 units — well below the unconstrained EOQ of 37,570 — resulting in an estimated annual cost saving of ~$3,478 (71.2%). Capacity utilisation at replenishment is near 100%, requiring close monitoring.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) Continuous-Review Reorder Point / Fixed Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Material PL1__M8952F4C has high-frequency, near-continuous demand (94.5% non-zero days) with moderate variability (CV=0.40), making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. It minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs via EOQ, while the fixed reorder point r ensures stock is replenished before the safety buffer is exhausted. Periodic review would add unnecessary latency given the stable, high-volume demand pattern.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage capacity of 22,674.9 units is binding: the optimal EOQ of 37,570 units cannot be placed in a single order without exceeding capacity after accounting for safety stock (1,579 units). The capped OQ of 21,095 units increases annual ordering frequency by ~78% vs. the unconstrained optimum, raising annual ordering cost from ~$580 to ~$1,034. Additionally, near-100% storage utilisation at each replenishment leaves no headroom for emergency stock or demand surges — a stockout risk during high-demand periods exists if an order is delayed.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility: MOQ (4,549) + safety_stock (1,579) = 6,128 < max_storage_units (22,674.9). However, management should assess whether storage capacity expansion is feasible, as it would unlock ~$450/year in additional ordering cost savings by enabling orders closer to the true EOQ.
